posts.name: 42-mind-gut-dopamine-taste
posts.caption:
Why does a taste you hated turn into one you crave? A slow signal from your gut to your brain may be part of the answer ☕

UCSF scientists found that nutrients in the stomach of mice trigger a dopamine wave in the amygdala that lasts minutes, not seconds. Block it and mice stop learning which flavors bring calories. Switch it on and they learn to like a flavor with no calories at all. Brain scans in people point to the same spot. Coffee itself was not tested.

Source: Grove, Knight et al. (UC San Francisco, Yale), “The neural basis of flavour-nutrient learning”, Nature, 2026.
